business_problem: Ramki Gaddipati, cofounder and CTO at Zeta, says, “We help banks rapidly scale critical capabilities such as real-time transaction processing, end-of-day processing, and always-on availability—delivering solutions that are reliable and cost-effective.” The Zeta platform went live on Amazon Web Services (AWS) in 2015.
solution_summary: Zeta’ s next-gen technology stack leverages cloud-native design principles to help banks achieve virtually infinite scalability and ironclad security in their digital strategies. As part of its platform's continued development, the company created a cloud-native architecture on AWS to optimize end-of-day processing. The team used Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run the services and scale them by processing Flink and Kafka platforms automatically. To complete the architecture, the team added Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for the platform’s database services and Amazon Athena to analyze petabytes of data from multiple sources. To optimize the EOD processing architecture’s storage for maximal performance, Zeta decided to use Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) Express One Zone , which Zeta’s tech team had discovered during AWS re:Invent .
